items.title: 56800_John Simmons oral history interview
items.q: Jimmy Hamilton had the clarinet solo and Oscar played rhythm and melody right along with him

ctx.x: base player. He loved me. It was, there was a nice sprinkling rankle of base players around town that could have played it just as well, I mean, but Oscar being a soloist, you know. They took him. I'll go along with it. Because I loved Oscar, you know, second to Blanton, solo wise.

Now I remember a record that he made with Duke that just gassed me, 'Airconditioned Jungle'. Jimmy Hamilton had the clarinet solo and Oscar played rhythm and melody right along with him, it was like a duet almost. He carried the melodic line and was playing the rhythm at the same time. And then this solo that he made on the cello Perdido'. Now that sounded like Charlie Christian on guitar almost.

And this solo that he made with Hawk and Eddie Heyward, 'The Man I Love', you could hear him breathing. Boy he could play. But now he's been not knowing anything about positions or tuning up or anything. He'd just pick up a bass, run his hand over it, find out where the notes was and he would hit it every time.
